completed: MPI-540 SHIPPED (ef3ebd2e). _doneCount had no expiry, so a batch whose queue never cleanly drained announced itself against a LATER drain - Fabio saw completion toasts 10-20 minutes late, once an hour late. Ruled out a downstream deferral FIRST: main.js showOsNotification fires on receipt and returns early when focused, and statusBar.js has no focus-deferred replay, so the count is the only thing that can carry a batch that far. This matters because Fabio's own theory was 'strip the come-back-when-unfocused thing' - that would have removed a working feature and left the bug. Fix: stamp _doneAt, drop a count older than 5 min, checked on BOTH edges (before counting a new completion AND at the top of _maybeArmFlush). A fire-time check alone is not enough - a fresh completion re-stamps the time and the orphans ride along as N+1.

MPI-539 failure 5 SHIPPED (a75c8a3e). _failOutstandingRemoteDeps terminated the DEPS but never the owning MODEL job - the one terminal path in downloadManager.js that did not call _checkModelJobsComplete(). Its dep-level download:failed carries no modelId and the client drops those by design (MPI-97), so nothing user-facing ever went terminal.

MPI-539 failure 6 SHIPPED (a75c8a3e). The client's serial install chain reads the engine when the POST lands, not when Install is pressed, so a queued install could fire against a different engine - Boogu would have put 20.8GB on Fabio's LOCAL disk unasked. A job now records the engine it was queued for and is DROPPED, never retargeted.

MPI-539 toast routing SHIPPED (5daac061), found DURING the live test. Fixing failure 5 made the failure reachable for the first time and it came up as the Report-on-GitHub dialog. Added a cause-agnostic `toast` verdict beside the existing networkBlocked/transient ones; both client branches join it to the arm that already shows data.error verbatim.

MPI-539 CLOSED on live evidence, recorded in tasks/MPI-539/validation.md. Fabio restarted the app, connected the CPU Pod, installed with a second queued behind, and stopped the Pod mid-download. Card reached a real end state; Model Library returned to LOCAL truth (his words: 'that's proven'); the queued SDXL NSFW cancelled with a named reason and did NOT download locally. Detection measured at 9s from app.log - the 90s stall watchdog never fired, and the lag he noticed is RunPod stopping the container, which he accepted.

MPI-541 REWRITTEN around its own disproof. Same 3.725 GiB box pulled the same model at up to 735 MB/s - above the 652 that supposedly OOMed it - with Telemetry reading 3% memory. Transport exonerated. App-side staging exonerated too: the app log shows MPI-539's abandon path firing by name in that session, so the getEngine fix was already live. (a) LOCAL: 'install blocked - disk full: need 29.3 GB free, have 29.4 GB at G:/CubricModels' - it had MORE than it asked for and blocked anyway, because routes/downloadManager.js:1684 gates on neededBytes * 1.05 while the message prints the un-margined number. Free up space and try again.', which names no disk and points at the wrong machine. Fix shape is already proven in this file: pass the server's message through, exactly as the networkBlocked / toast arms do. js/services/downloadService.js ~line 637 and ~665 hold the two _isOutOfSpaceError branches that overwrite it.

next_action.description: Fix the disk-space message. Two confirmed instances in today's app.log, both quoted in this handoff's pending list. Pass the server's precise message through instead of overwriting it - the pattern already exists in the same function (the networkBlocked / toast arms show data.error verbatim), so this is the third use of a proven shape, not a new mechanism. Make the LOCAL message print the margin-inclusive requirement so the number matches the decision, and stop the REMOTE case saying 'free up space' when the full disk is the Pod volume. That fix is the last open item on the MPI-542 umbrella besides MPI-540's confirmation - once the umbrella is clear, cut 1.4.1.

key_decisions: Did NOT strip the focus-based notification routing, even though Fabio asked for it. Checked main.js and statusBar.js first: nothing downstream defers, so stripping it would have removed a working feature and left the bug untouched. Said so in one line and fixed the actual carrier. The lesson generalises - his theory named a real-sounding mechanism that measurably was not there.

MPI-540 keeps the coalescing. Deleting it was the laziest fix and would have returned per-gen notification spam on a queue of N, which is the bug coalescing was added to fix. A 5-minute expiry keeps both.

The staleness window is wall-clock, not a batch id. A batch id threaded from the queue would be exact but means a new field through generationService and commandExecutor. Marked with a ponytail: comment naming the ceiling - the visible cost is an undercount when one batch has a >5min gap between items.

MPI-541 was NOT closed and NOT fixed speculatively. Three healthy runs at up to 735 MB/s on a 4 GB box mean the OOM is not a reproducible property of the download path, so capping HF_XET_NUM_CONCURRENT_RANGE_GETS would be a fix for a cause nobody has evidence for. Reopen criteria recorded instead.

The `toast` verdict is deliberately cause-agnostic, unlike networkBlocked and transient which each name a specific condition. It means 'show this exact message as a toast' so any future server-side path can reach the same routing without a new client branch.
MPI-541 stayed a separate card rather than folding into MPI-539: different root, different repo (mpi-ci), and it would OOM the same box with no app bug at all.

1.4.1, not 1.5.0, and the whole scratchpad folds together. Fabio's first instruction was that anything already unreleased belonged to 1.5 and only today's fixes to 1.4.1, so the file was split by target; he then looked at what was actually in it and collapsed that - there are no real features pending, so it is all one patch. The split was removed rather than left in place 'just in case': two live targets in one scratchpad is exactly the shape that shipped 1.4.0's bullets twice.
constraints: A routes/ change does NOT survive a renderer reload - the app needs a full restart. This cost one wasted test cycle today; Fabio re-ran the same drill against the old code before we caught it.

js/services/downloadService.js CANNOT import in bare Node: MpiButton.js imports an absolute '/js/utils/icons.js' which resolves to c:\js\utils\icons.js. Its guard is therefore a SOURCE-READ test that pins the guard's position ahead of the POST. js/shell/notificationService.js DOES import with DOM stubs - see tests/notification-stale-count.test.cjs for the stub set.
routes/downloadManager.js exports _modelJobs and _depJobs for unit tests only (added this session, matching the file's existing test-only export convention). Never mutate them outside tests.
Fabio's app owns :3000. Do not drive it, do not restart it.
The Pod volume is ~140GB used of 150GB, so a large install will legitimately hit the remote disk gate. That is not a bug - it is what produced today's second disk-message instance.
Board enum traps that cost three validator round-trips: `maturity: seed` is invalid despite existing on live cards, and a `done` card needs `status: completed`.
